title: Upper/mid/lower thoracic axial twist ROM at max twist and with neutral vs flexed lumbar spine (standing)
condition: healthy, standing, maximal right twist and combined lumbar posture / thoracic twist

quantity.name: regional thoracic axial twist ROM
quantity.definition: axial angle change between proximal and distal marker plates of each region, upright to held right-twist posture

source.sample: 13 males; 13 right-handed males free of neck, back and shoulder pain for >= 1 year (university population)

protocol.summary: Max twist ≈ evenly shared (11.8/15.2/11.2 deg); lumbar flexion reduces mid-thoracic twist by ~5 deg.
how_to_use: For standing maximal twist distribute thoracic axial rotation ≈ 31% T1-T4, 40% T5-T8, 29% T9-T12.
When the lumbar spine is pre-flexed (~50%), reduce mid-thoracic twist by ~5 deg (15.0 -> 10.0 deg).

measurement.device: Vicon MX 50 Hz; rigid 3-marker plates on spinous processes defining T1-T4, T5-T8, T9-T12 and L1-PSIS segments; regional angle between proximal and distal plates
measurement.task: max forward flexion; max right axial twist; ~50% lumbar flexion or neutral lumbar combined with thoracic flexion (chin to chest) or right thoracic twist; 5 s hold

extraction.from: Results text (7 of 9 values with SD); Fig 3 (upper-thoracic bars of the two combined postures)
extraction.uncertainty: text values as printed; 2 digitised means ±0.2 deg
extraction.check_notes: Fig 3 calibrated on the 7 text means (reproduced within 0.07 deg). Fig 3 error bars do NOT match the text SDs (e.g. max-twist upper thoracic: whisker ≈3.2 deg vs text SD 6.70), so SDs of the 2 digitised bars are left null.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
